newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas slides on stock build.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas slides on stock build.

text.p: Gasoline ended lower for the fourth day running on news of a sharp build in Singapore stocks as sellers searched for new outlets, traders said on Thursday.
Light distillate stocks in Singapore for the week ending April 9 rose to a near two-year high at 7.237 million barrels, up 855,000 barrels from the previous week, the Trade Development Board said.
The stocks comprise gasoline, reformate and naphtha.
"Things are not looking good," one trader said.
Traders said there are not many buyers despite the upcoming summer driving season in the northern hemisphere.
"The only demand is in Japan, but even they are not buying much," one seller said.
Earlier talks of demand from Australia due to scheduled refinery maintenance there in the second quarter were shortlived as Australian refiners quickly covered their requirements.
"We only need small volume for Australia, and they are not in a hurry to buy," a refining source said.
The market is looking to Taiwan for incremental demand in the hope that the next tender for second half May cargoes might soak up more of the surplus availabilties.
In the local spot market no 95-octane unleaded cargoes were offered with attention diverted to 97 and 92 octane.
One 97-octane cargo was offered down to a low of $26.30 per barrel but no buyers emerged, a sharp contrast to the $27.60 traded level for a 95-octane cargo on April 2.
Traders said 92-octane was offered at $25.20 again not eliciting any buying interest.
Naphtha swaps fell sharply in response to lower prices in Japan as the market gave up its early week gains.
May was last quoted at $21.30/$21.50 per barrel from $21.70/$21.90 on Wednesday.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
